title: Wafer-scale single-crystal graphene synthesis
bottleneck: Graphene's remarkable properties belong to pristine single crystals, but wafer-scale synthesis still yields polycrystalline films whose grain boundaries degrade electrical and mechanical performance. Epitaxial growth on silicon carbide is high quality but limited in size and expensive; CVD on copper is scalable but defect-prone, and transfer processes introduce wrinkles, tears, and contamination. No method yet delivers meter-scale, defect-free, transferable graphene at commodity cost.
why_it_blocks: Graphene was supposed to revolutionize electronics, composites, and membranes. The synthesis gap means real products use graphene as a filler or additive — incremental improvements — while the transformative applications needing pristine large-area films stay on the shelf.
current_state: Roll-to-roll CVD now produces kilometers of few-layer graphene for heating films and touch sensors, proving some markets work with imperfect material. But the high-end applications that motivated the field still wait on crystal quality at scale.
